Prompts: Prepare a bottle filled with water containing suspended iron filings. Bring two magnets close to opposite sides of the bottle.

Author: Lanxiang Hu
Expected phenomenon: The magnet swings toward the aluminum plates but slows down quickly and does not complete as many oscillations as expected, showing significant damping of motion.
Prompts: Tie a neodymium magnet to a string so it can swing freely like a pendulum. Place aluminum plates beneath it, leaving a small gap at the lowest point of the swing. Pull the magnet to about a 45 degree angle, then release it.

Author: Lanxiang Hu
Expected phenomenon: The water doesn’t not leak.
Prompts: Pierce a pencil through the water-filled section of a plastic bag filled with water and out the other side, while keeping the pencil in place.

Author: Daniel Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The light starts lighting up and flashing after the person turns the handle
Keywords: Energy Conversion, Rotational Dynamics, Simple circuit lighting
Prompts: A person is standing next to a brown table with a hand-crank that is connected to a generator and a light bulb. He begins continuously turning the hand-crank.

Author: Daniel Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The car runs into the spring, the spring compresses slightly, then sends the car a little bit back up the ramp.
Keywords: Angular Momentum, Elastic Collision, Energy Conversion, Gravity
Prompts: A toy car is released from rest at the top of an inclined ramp. At the bottom of the ramp, a spring is fixed so that the car rolls straight into it. The spring's orientation is parallel to the ramp.

Example Title: Velcro-Coupled Collision Between Two Identical Carts
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: After impact, the two carts stick and move together in the original direction at a slower speed.
Keywords: Inelastic Collision, Kinetic Energy Loss, Momentum Conservation
Prompts: Two identical-mass carts sit on a low-friction track. Both carts have Velcro pads facing each other. The left cart is held still by hand; the right cart is pushed toward it with an initial speed.

Example Title: Head-On Velcro Collision Between Two Identical Carts
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: The two carts approach, collide, and stick together at the center. Because their momenta are equal and opposite, the combined object remains at rest after collision.
Keywords: Inelastic Collision, Kinetic Energy Loss, Momentum Conservation
Prompts: Two identical-mass carts sit on a low-friction track. Both carts have Velcro pads facing each other. Both carts are pushed toward each other at the same speed.

Example Title: A Billiard Ball Rolling Inside a Ring
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: The ball no longer experiences the inward centripetal force and moves straight along the tangent direction from the point where it lost contact with the ring.
Prompts: A billiard ball is placed inside a circular ring and rolled along the inner wall so that it moves continuously in a circular path. While the ball is rolling, the ring is suddenly lifted upward, removing the circular constraint.

Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: After adding the powder, the yellow turmeric solution turns reddish-brown.
Prompts: A glass of water is prepared, and a small amount of turmeric powder is added and stirred until the solution turns yellow. Then, a spoonful of surf excel powder is added and mixed.

Example Title: A Ball Launched Upward at an Angle from a Table Edge
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: The ball first rises and then falls along a curved parabolic path, traveling forward before hitting the ground.
Prompts: A small rubber ball is launched diagonally upward from the edge of a table using a slanted ramp.

Example Title: Two Balls Released from the Same Height
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: Both balls hit the ground at the same time because their vertical motions are identical. The ball that rolled off the table lands farther horizontally since it has a non-zero horizontal velocity, while the dropped ball lands directly below its release point.
Prompts: A small ball rolls horizontally off the right edge of a table. At the same instant and from the same height, a second identical ball is released from rest directly above the floor.

Example Title: Place A Penny on a Turntable
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: At first, friction keeps the penny still on the turntable. Over time, it directly slips out of the turntable.
Prompts: A penny is placed near the center of a turntable, then start spinning the turntable.

Example Title: A Ball Dropped Off-Center on a Spinning Turntable
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: When the ball touches the spinning surface off-center, it immediately flies outward.
Prompts: A ball is dropped onto a spinning turntable, not at its center but near the outer region.

Example Title: Holding and Releasing a Ball on a Spinning Turntable
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: After being released, the ball stays in its position relative to the spinning surface, it continues rotating with the same angular speed and does not slide outward.
Prompts: A ball is held at a fixed position on a spinning turntable. After the turntable reaches a steady speed, the ball is gently released without pushing it.

Example Title: Head-On Magnetic Collision Between Two Identical Carts
Author: Haoyang Yu
Expected phenomenon: As the two carts approach, magnetic repulsion decelerates both equally until they momentarily stop near the center. Then, they reverse direction and move away with the same speed in opposite directions.
Prompts: Two identical carts with magnets of opposite poles facing each other are placed on a frictionless track. Both carts are released simultaneously and move toward each other at equal speed.

Example Title: Laser Vanishes Between Crossed Polarizers with Tape
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The dark field brightens where the tape sits because the film rotates polarization and creates constructive transmission patterns.
Prompts: Arrange two linear polarizers orthogonal to each other and shine a small laser spot through them, then insert a piece of transparent tape between the sheets.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The balloon sticks by electrostatic attraction and later falls as charge dissipates.
Prompts: Rub a latex balloon on cloth and press it onto a painted wall.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: Condensation forms then clears as the film evaporates, restoring a sharp reflection with subtle color tints.
Prompts: Chill a metal spoon, breathe onto the surface, and hold it under a bright lamp.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: With insufficient speed the marble leaves the track at the top and follows a free-flight arc.
Prompts: Send a marble through a vertical loop track with adjustable entry speed.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The speckle texture appears to drift opposite to the card motion because of phase interference.
Prompts: Shine a laser on a diffuse card and slide the card laterally while keeping the dot centered in frame.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: Colorful stress fringes appear and change with rotation as polarization components shift.
Prompts: Place a clear plastic fork between crossed polarizers and rotate the fork slowly.

Example Title: Magnet Slow Slide on Aluminum Ramp
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The magnet creeps slowly due to eddy-current drag while the steel block slides freely.
Prompts: Compare a strong magnet and a steel block sliding down the same aluminum ramp.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: Concentric colored fringes emerge as a Newton’s ring pattern from path‑length differences.
Prompts: Press two glass plates together with a small droplet between them and illuminate with white light.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The beam becomes trapped by total internal reflection and forms bright nodes along the path where partial scattering interferes.
Prompts: Send a thin laser sheet into the edge of a clear acrylic block and adjust entry angle along the long face.

Example Title: Water Jet Deflected Near Charged Comb with Laser Sheet
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The lit jet bows toward the comb while still descending, making the curved path obvious as charge polarizes the water.
Prompts: Create a thin water jet from a bottle nozzle, illuminate it with a laser sheet, and bring a charged plastic comb close to the stream.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The screen brightness and the reflected glare extinguish at different angles because emitted polarization and reflected polarization do not match.
Prompts: Place a linear polarizer over a phone screen showing a white field and rotate the sheet while observing a glossy reflection of a lamp.

Example Title: Angular Momentum Surprise with Collapsing Props
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The rotation speeds up and the platform resists external twists because the moment of inertia decreases while angular momentum stays constant.
Prompts: Spin a turntable with two sliding masses near the rim and move the masses inward along radial tracks.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The series-spring system oscillates with a noticeably longer period because the effective spring constant is reduced.
Keywords: Gravity, Hooke’s law, Simple harmonic motion
Prompts: Mount a mass from one vertical spring and compare its oscillation to the same mass hung from two identical springs in series.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The pattern suddenly jumps from one mode shape to another as the length tunes through resonance conditions set by tension and elasticity.
Prompts: Drive a taut string with a small motor at a fixed frequency and slide a movable support to change the effective length.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The magnet slows dramatically over copper sections yet speeds up over plastic, tracing a stop–go motion from eddy-current drag changes.
Prompts: Construct a metal ramp with alternating copper and plastic strips and slide a strong magnet from the top.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The beam shimmers and bends due to temperature-dependent index variations that act like moving lenses in the air.
Prompts: Create a warm air plume from a candle beside a cool background and pass a laser pointer’s beam just above the flame.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: A stable vortex forms and the water drains faster and smoothly because the rotating core lowers central pressure and keeps an air passage.
Prompts: Fill a plastic bottle with water, puncture a vent hole near the top, and swirl the bottle while uncapping to let water drain.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: Moving bands of vivid color appear as thickness gradients cause wavelength-dependent constructive and destructive interference with mirror reflections.
Prompts: Spray a very thin soap film onto a small mirror and illuminate with white light at a shallow angle.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: Only one LED lights depending on polarity and contact pressure; contact resistance modulates brightness without adding components.
Prompts: Wire two LEDs in opposite directions across a coin cell using copper tape and gently press a paper flap as a switch.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: Shimmering distortions and apparent bending of submerged edges occur as cold brine pockets with higher refractive index form and sink during melting.
Prompts: Place ice cubes and a spoonful of salt in a clear glass of water and observe through the side as the mixture is gently stirred once.

Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The cone appears to roll uphill while its center of mass actually moves downward along the widening rails.
Prompts: Set two rails in a V-shape that spread apart upward and place a double cone at the low end; nudge the cone gently along the rails.

Example Title: Raw vs Cooked Egg Spin Test
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The raw egg starts spinning again due to the fluid interior continuing to move, while the cooked egg remains at rest.
Prompts: Spin a raw egg and a cooked egg on a smooth surface; lightly stop each with a fingertip and then release.

Example Title: Compass Deflection by Simple Wire Loop
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: The compass needle swings away from north while the current flows, indicating the magnetic field around the loop.
Prompts: Place a small compass at the center of a single-turn wire loop and briefly connect the loop to a coin cell.

Example Title: Electrostatic Shielding with Cup and Foil
Author: Yujie Zhao
Expected phenomenon: External charged objects brought near the cup produce little response inside, showing field shielding by the conductor.
Prompts: Wrap the outside of a paper cup with aluminum foil connected to ground and place a small electroscope leaf inside the cup opening.
